stories.title: Nvidia’s biggest RAM supplier just had a trillion-dollar debut on Wall Street
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: SK Hynix, a major RAM supplier, successfully debuted on Wall Street.
The IPO was massive, raising $26.5 billion and surpassing Alibaba's record for a foreign company debut.
The event highlights the surging demand for memory chips driven by the ongoing AI boom.

stories.title: Disable auto-play and infinite scroll or risk massive fines, EU tells Meta
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: The EU's Digital Services Act (DSA) is compelling Meta to alter platform functionalities.
Key required changes include disabling auto-play and infinite scroll features.
Non-compliance with these regulations could result in substantial financial penalties for Meta.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the active LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
Key technologies associated include transformers, safetensors, and the Llama architecture.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It points to the use of standard NLP pipelines like 'text-generation' for this model.
The associated tags indicate relevance to transformers, safetensors, and the Llama family of models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and 8VC.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speed improvement using the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in higher quality model outputs.
The updates also lead to faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating local LLM execution into the personal AI agent ecosystem.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads on Mac devices.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating active development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with existing messaging applications.
It connects these apps to local AI coding agents.
A key feature is that all AI processing runs entirely on the user's local device for privacy.

stories.title: Would you host part of an AI data center in your home?
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Sunrun is piloting a 'distributed AI compute' program.
The program involves paying customers to host compute units in their homes.
This represents a novel approach to scaling AI data center capacity outside of traditional centralized facilities.

stories.title: OpenAI wants its new tool to do your work for you and with you
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: OpenAI is developing a new tool, rebranded as Codex, designed to automate and assist in user workflows.
The new capability suggests a move towards more autonomous AI agents capable of sustained, long-running tasks.
This development signals a significant industry shift toward integrated, persistent AI assistants rather than simple prompt-response models.

stories.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
stories.author: Jugal Kalita
bullet_points: Introduces AUTOPILOT-VQA, a new benchmark specifically designed for incident-centric visual question answering in dashcam video.
Addresses a critical gap in current research: reliably evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for safety-critical incident reasoning in autonomous driving.
Leverages recent advancements in VLMs and LLMs to push the boundaries of autonomous vehicle scene understanding and decision-making.

stories.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs
stories.author: Carson K. Leung
bullet_points: Traditional LLM evaluation (accuracy/perplexity) is insufficient for assessing quantization effects.
The paper introduces 'correctness agreement,' a new decision-level metric to measure behavioral changes post-quantization.
This research addresses a critical gap in deploying LLMs efficiently in resource-constrained environments.

stories.title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
stories.author: Davis Rempe
bullet_points: ARDY introduces a new autoregressive diffusion model for generating realistic 3D human motions.
The research addresses the critical trade-off between the high controllability of offline motion generation and the real-time inference speed needed for interactive applications.
The hybrid representation aims to improve both the semantic understanding (text/goals) and the temporal coherence of generated motions.

stories.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
stories.author: Xihui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces UniClawBench, a new universal benchmark designed to evaluate proactive agents.
Addresses limitations of existing benchmarks, which often use sandboxed environments and single-turn evaluation.
Aims to provide a more rigorous evaluation framework for LLMs and multimodal models operating in real-world tasks.

stories.title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces 'WebSwarm,' a new framework for recursive multi-agent orchestration to enhance LLM-based web search.
Addresses limitations of single ReAct agents, which struggle with balancing search depth and breadth.
Aims to overcome existing multi-agent system constraints, particularly regarding recursive depth and coverage.

stories.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
stories.author: Zhiyuan Liu
bullet_points: Addresses the diminishing returns of scaling laws as training data approaches physical limits.
Proposes 'UltraX,' a method for refining pre-training data at scale using adaptive programmatic editing.
Aims to overcome limitations of existing refinement techniques (rule-based, LLM-based) in quality and efficiency.

stories.title: It Takes a MAESTRO To Prune Bad Experts
stories.author: Tanmoy Chakraborty
bullet_points: Addresses the deployment bottleneck in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where full expert banks remain in memory despite sparse activation.
Introduces MAESTRO, a new method designed to prune 'bad experts' in MoE models.
Overcomes limitations of existing pruning methods by accounting for the interdependent nature of MoE routing, unlike heuristics designed for dense transformers.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance enhancements and broader GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to expand model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows in AI applications.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Disney Plus is reportedly looking into a free streaming tier
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Disney Plus is reportedly exploring the implementation of a free streaming tier.
The idea was mentioned by Adam Smith, Disney's chief product and technology officer, during a company town hall.
The specific content that would be available on a potential free tier remains unclear.

stories.title: Instagram’s Adam Mosseri: If you don’t like AI, ‘then you shouldn’t have it in your feed’
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Instagram head Adam Mosseri advocates against filtering out AI-generated content on the platform.
Mosseri suggests that users who dislike AI content should actively manage what appears in their feeds.
The discussion highlights the ongoing debate regarding content moderation and the integration of AI into social media feeds.

stories.title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
stories.author: Hongsheng Li
bullet_points: Introduces OpenCoF, a method designed to enable reasoning within video generation models.
Proposes Chain-of-Frame (CoF) reasoning as a novel way for models to unfold logical consequences across temporally connected video frames.
Addresses the limitation of current video generators, which lack specific supervision for dedicated CoF reasoning despite being trained on general corpora.

stories.title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
stories.author: Xue Yang
bullet_points: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a new benchmark designed to test AI's ability to understand scientific lineage.
Addresses the gap in current AI evaluation by modeling scientific ideas as having an 'inheritance structure,' similar to biological genomes.
Focuses on benchmarking scientific lineage reasoning and generating new ideas grounded in prior research.

stories.title: Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis
stories.author: Valerie Heckel
bullet_points: The study provides a large-scale, objective analysis of AI learning assistant usage (Syntea) in higher education.
It analyzes usage patterns across diverse student demographics, including gender, age, and degree.
The research addresses a gap in existing literature by using large-scale log data rather than small surveys.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The research explores the internal k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed by UMAP, a widely used dimensionality reduction technique.
The study argues that this internal graph retains crucial information about the high-dimensional data manifold before projection distortion.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this pre-projection graph can enhance data sensemaking beyond typical UMAP visualization workflows.

stories.title: Workflow as Knowledge: Semantic Persistence for LLM-Mediated Workflows
stories.author: Francesco Zanitti
bullet_points: Proposes a language-independent conceptual model for managing LLM-mediated workflows.
Focuses on 'Semantic Persistence' to better handle complex workflow elements like tool use and branching.
Utilizes Lisp-inspired concepts (symbolic forms, object identity) as explanatory frameworks rather than strict implementation rules.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: The research introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically trained for European Portuguese.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like defining the moral foundation of authority.
The study cautions that high agreement (reliability) does not guarantee validity when inferring complex theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical insights.
A new lightweight temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge the gap between pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The technology has relevance across fields like rehabilitation, sports science, ergonomics, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Score Accuracy Along the Forward Diffusion Does Not Certify Numerical Stability in Diffusion Sampling
stories.author: Yiwei Zhou
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that low forward-marginal error in score matching guarantees numerical stability during diffusion sampling.
It demonstrates that a smooth score field with arbitrarily small forward error can still lead to a nonexplosive and stable reverse-time process.
This highlights a critical distinction between theoretical error bounds (forward marginals) and practical stability during iterative sampling (reverse trajectory).

stories.title: SLORR: Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
stories.author: Shiwei Liu
bullet_points: SLORR introduces a new technique for in-training low-rank regularization to improve neural network compressibility.
It addresses limitations of existing methods, such as the need for SVDs of large matrices or architectural modifications.
The proposed method is highlighted as being simple, stateless, and efficient.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The paper explores the underutilized k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed internally by UMAP.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, unlike the final 2D projection.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this latent graph can enhance data sensemaking beyond typical UMAP usage.

stories.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
stories.author: Akarsha Sehwag
bullet_points: Identifies 'Super Weights' in LLMs—parameters whose removal drastically degrades model performance.
Challenges the universal applicability of Super Weight importance across all LLMs.
Demonstrates that training Super Weights in isolation is counterproductive, causing accuracy to drop to random levels.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical insights.
A new lightweight plug-in temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge pose estimation with biomechanical attribute prediction.
The technology has significant potential applications in fields like rehabilitation, sports science, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
stories.author: Abhishek Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of transferring flexible, language-based reasoning capabilities from LLMs to continuous control policies.
Proposes a novel framework, 'Latent Memory Palace,' utilizing Autoregressive Variational Inference to structure decision-making.
Aims to bridge the gap between high-level linguistic reasoning and the granular spatial understanding required for precise robotic control.

stories.title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
stories.author: Barath Raghavan
bullet_points: Proposes LTM, a large-scale terrain model designed for wildfire-prone landscapes.
Addresses the limitations of existing methods: LiDAR is expensive/infrequent, while image-based methods struggle with sparse features.
Introduces a multi-modal reconstruction framework to improve terrain mapping accuracy for emergency response.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like defining the moral foundation of authority.
The research highlights the critical distinction between agreement (reliability) and validity when using LLMs for complex theoretical annotation.

stories.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Zhuokai Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses 'behavioral state decay' in long-horizon AI tasks where critical information gets lost in large trajectories.
Proposes treating memory not as passive retrieval, but as an active intervention mechanism for decision-making.
Focuses on enabling agents to surface scattered, decision-relevant state (facts, goals, prior attempts) as tasks become complex.

stories.title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
stories.author: Kevin Paul
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need to benchmark LLM judges used as reward models in reinforcement learning, specifically for citation verification.
It focuses on the calibration and bias of LLMs when assessing citation quality in deep-research systems that require source attribution for every claim.
This research is highly relevant to the reliability and trustworthiness of advanced, search-grounded LLMs.

stories.title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Jyh-Shing Roger Jang
bullet_points: Introduces 'DominoTree,' a new method for conditional tree-structured drafting to enhance speculative decoding in LLMs.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods (like DDTree) by incorporating a GRU-based causal correction for path-dependent draft token distributions.
Aims to accelerate LLM inference by improving the accuracy and structure of the draft tokens used in speculative decoding.

stories.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
stories.author: Jonathan Amar
bullet_points: Analyzes real-world patient-chatbot conversations (2,053) to reveal high variability in communication patterns and emotional expression.
Highlights a critical limitation in current chatbot development: over-reliance on cooperative, simulated patients.
Introduces a novel patient simulator designed to model distinct aspects of patient interaction, including clinical content and emotional state.

stories.title: Cpp2Rust: Automatic Translation of C++ to Safe Rust
stories.author: github.com via gnyeki
bullet_points: Cpp2Rust is a project focused on automatically translating C++ codebases into Rust.
The primary goal is to leverage Rust's memory safety features while migrating existing C++ infrastructure.
This addresses the growing need for safer, modern systems programming languages in large codebases.

stories.title: Return on Attention: Why AI Code Reviews Are Wearing Us Out
stories.author: cseeman
bullet_points: AI code reviews are leading to increased PR volume without corresponding improvements in ticket quality.
The review process is becoming heavily automated, with LLMs participating in reviews and generating responses.
The underlying issue identified is broader than just code review, suggesting a systemic problem in development workflows.

stories.title: Make AI Agents See Your Website
stories.author: kumakint
bullet_points: AI coding agents are becoming integrated into the standard developer workflow.
The article discusses the growing presence and impact of these AI agents on development practices.
The topic focuses on enabling AI agents to interact with and 'see' live websites.

stories.title: Are You Using Coding Agents Like Slot Machines?
stories.author: loicboset
bullet_points: Coding agents are significantly accelerating software development timelines.
The article raises a cautionary question about the dependency and reliability of these tools.
It reflects the current industry push towards broader AI adoption in development workflows.

stories.title: I Built a Linter That Catches the Security Bugs AI Assistants Keep Writing
stories.author: ri5hu
bullet_points: The article discusses the use of AI assistants (Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude) in software development.
The author developed a custom linter specifically designed to identify security vulnerabilities introduced by AI-generated code.
This highlights a growing industry concern regarding the security risks associated with relying on generative AI for coding tasks.
